title: Viewport-only layout tests miss the actual containing boundary

scenario.observed_change: A responsive layout passes a narrow-viewport regression, but a desktop media rule imposes fixed minimum grid tracks that exceed the actual reader column once surrounding navigation and table-of-contents chrome reduce available width.
controlled_inputs: reader container width after surrounding chrome
authority_boundaries: viewport dimensions versus the effective layout container
isolated component sizing versus the real consumer page chrome
operation_model: verify the component at a narrow viewport where the desktop rule is inactive
open the real desktop Site layout with side chrome
activate fixed desktop track minimums against a narrower reader column
component overflows horizontally despite the green mobile regression

required_invariants.requirement: Resource and layout boundaries must be tested at the effective containing boundary when that boundary, rather than viewport width alone, determines correctness.

must_investigate: which container actually constrains the component at the affected breakpoint
whether existing browser coverage activates the desktop rule in the real page chrome
must_identify: viewport-only coverage does not prove shrinkability inside the effective desktop reader container
must_not_claim: responsive safety from a mobile-only assertion that never activates the failing desktop rule
sufficient width from viewport size when surrounding chrome reduces the actual component container

provenance.note: Codex found that fixed desktop grid minima could overflow the Site reader column even though the supplied 360px browser assertion passed because it never activated the desktop media rule.
